r0.why: Group of rock-forming aluminium tectosilicates with other cations, the two common members and the 60%/41% by-weight figures are all in 1-3.

r1.why: Crystallizing from magma as intrusive and extrusive igneous rock, presence in metamorphic and sedimentary rock, and anorthosite are in 4-6.

r2.why: Feldspat from Feld and Spat, Spat's long use for easily cleaved rock, 18th-century introduction and the English spar influence are in 7-9.

r3.why: Aluminosilicate tetrahedra, Al or Si with four oxygens, shared oxygens forming a 3D network, and open space for Na, K, Ca giving charge balance are in 34-36 and 39.

r4.why: Calcium-rich plagioclase first, growing sodium-rich, K-feldspar last are in 18 and 20; 'not all at once' follows directly.

r5.why: Hydrolysis to illite, smectite, kaolinite; dissolving best in acid or base; dissolution rate controlling weathering; reaction with H+ or OH-; clay abundance are in 40-43 and 45.

r6.why: Perthite from exsolution on cooling of an intermediate composition, naked-eye visibility in many granites, and labradorite colour play from fine exsolution lamellae (Boggild intergrowth) are in 23, 24, 32.
